skills.degradedBehavior: Delivery review retains its declared bound; plan review is unbounded and may end by operator decision.
Decomposition remains complete and reports the undecomposed candidates plus every omitted mutation when the host-native tracker capability is unavailable.
Decomposition remains complete and reports the undecomposed candidates plus every omitted mutation when the host-native tracker capability is unavailable.
Optional tracking remains optional; declared product recovery must reconcile saved context and unresolved actions before evidence reuse.

Without a configuration the views are not declared and the core workflow's built-in pages remain; a view that cannot read a run, a report or a snapshot shows it as unavailable rather than failing the render. Recovered landing times use source occurrence, while the activity feed retains observation time. Unknown phase times remain unavailable; configured forge templates recognize validated cross-repository pull requests with compact labels and retained repository identity. Native review observations retain actual reports without a run; missing or candidate-mismatched artifacts stay unavailable and carry no admission authority. Originating closure explanations remain available through a collapsed keyboard-accessible disclosure, with settlement summaries visible. Without a plan.json the line map is unchanged; one that can't be read adds only the plan chapter with a flag naming its key path. A plan without planReview or a blocking approval draws exactly as before. A record without a lead check selection draws the checking panel as before. Before hand-off a planned story's round cards and notes come from the capture of its latest journaled round; a planned story with no round yet says when its rounds will appear. Without the supervisor's needs-you.json the Now chapter has no Needs you box; a list from a stopped supervisor, one a pass overdue, or one that can't be read is shown as unavailable, never stale. A round card says when an approval carried deferrable notes, and gives each deferral why it waited, from the rule that let it, and how it ended, from its own lens's later rounds only; its failure scenario, proposed change, follow-up and round history open on a click. The line map labels a carried check, a flaky base run and a peer's merge in its feed. Owned hosted publishing starts or adopts an independent generation-aware watcher, bounds terminal close publication to 30 seconds, retains pending terminal cuts for ten-minute retries and supports credential-free archive viewing with explicit archive retry. Hosted publishing is qualified from exact built archive bytes in two independently configured adopters; the separately deployed viewer and its dependencies are excluded from workflow archives. A record with no story shows its chapters without one. The hosted page shows what the local live view shows, from the same record, story, every entry's facts and the integration step included; a cut holding a configured secret's value or a credential-named field is refused with its code, a sibling's hosted link, which grants read access to that delivery, is left out as a credential, and another snapshot or renderer version is refused. Without --scope or --status-state the Jira snapshot reads every child of the parent by its status category, as before; a scoped snapshot lists another repository's children as outside, and the line map shows them only in a collapsed Elsewhere fold. A sibling delivery that can't be reached, redirects or times out reads as unavailable, and one with another renderer version or a body that fails its digest, fingerprint or schema check reads as incompatible; a cut the service calls stale reads as stale unless it is a confirmed terminal cut, and none of these changes the sibling's stories. A record with no siblings draws as before; with siblings, every view adds a folded Across repositories group per sibling, each saying since when it has shown no change, or its outcome since that outcome began, or that it was never read, and an outside child a sibling holds is drawn in its group rather than under Elsewhere. Once every own story has landed, a sibling with open work, one never read or one not fresh keeps the done headline away: the views say this repository's part is done and name each such sibling. With a same-epic sibling the line map's main line runs on past this repository's finish line to a post for the epic, whose count covers every same-epic sibling's stories; at most two siblings, those this repository waits on and then the furthest behind, turn in from rows under the lanes, and the rest fold into a "+N more" chip. A sibling that can't be read turns in dotted and turns the epic's line and post dashed and neutral, labelled "Epic ?" and naming it, with no warning colour. A sibling of another epic draws nothing on the line and is named in the chapter under an "Also linked" row. When the record has region claims, the line map's Who's doing what chapter offers a Who holds which files view, closed by default, read from the record and lane-changes.json: each claimed file solid where its lane has changed it and hollow where it hasn't, each shared file split by its lanes' line stretches, and a shared file's reading with each lane's stretches, changes and changed functions; a lane whose branch can't be read is shown so, and with no region claims the page has no such view. On a delivery with an integration target, the line map's count line under the delivery's name reads in two beats naming the target, its drift and the catch-ups, the line runs on past the integration base through the target merged in, the suite, the review and the change request into the target, and a Before it rejoins ledger pins each proof to the head it was taken at and strikes one a newer head supersedes; a delivery without one renders as before. While a delivery rejoins its target, the line draws that step in place of the epic's post. Without a git identity in its checkout the local line map's corner shows only the theme switch, and the hosted page never carries one; the files view stays hidden until a branch read lists a file or fails.
Execution remains complete and reports every omitted tracking mutation when the host-native tracker capability is unavailable.
Execution remains complete and reports every omitted tracking mutation when the host-native tracker capability is unavailable.

Optional tracking and sensors may be absent; declared product gates and recovery remain authoritative and cannot be replaced with executor-invented evidence. Unsupported v2 reporting remains explicit; retain selected output without changing delivery authority. Terminal handoffs retain the bound review release identity and any release installed mid-review. Shared sensor resources follow the declared allocation; explicit caller scope remains authoritative for stale test pins.

Core delivery remains complete and reports that the knowledge library was not consulted when the host's hive-mined server is unavailable or the repository declares no knowledge properties. The adapter is read-only; the properties document is a read-only input and is never guessed.

Core delivery remains complete and reports omitted optional tracking when the host-native Jira capability is unavailable. schemaVersion identifies the properties document; operational properties remain read-only inputs.

Core delivery remains complete and reports omitted optional tracking when the host-native Linear capability is unavailable. schemaVersion identifies the properties document; operational properties remain read-only inputs.

Native subagent dispatch and aggregation remain available without Python helpers; unavailable lenses remain explicit acquisition states. Unsupported v2 reporting remains explicit; retain selected output without changing delivery authority. Every host-convention lens uses a separate verified candidate checkout; unavailable isolation remains explicit. Base-move replay identity compares delivered path and line bytes, independent of shifted hunk positions or context.

Without a host that can start and message sessions no lane starts: the lead records the blocker and brings it to the operator, who may choose to deliver the tickets one at a time through $execute-work. Optional tracking may be absent; the delivery state and journal remain authoritative for where the epic stands. Recovered merges preserve source occurrence separately from observation; unavailable source times remain unknown. Native review observations retain actual reports without a run; missing or candidate-mismatched artifacts stay unavailable and carry no admission authority. Ready and merge hooks receive an exact runner-derived single or batch check mode; it carries no admission authority. Without selection.lead in the binding, or without a lead selection for the candidate's reviewed head, the provider selects its checks as before. Without bases in the binding, the runner serves its base.ref alone. Integration close-out restores the target binding and generation before review. Before hand-off a planned story has no head, so its observation is bound to the capture of its latest journaled round, and a later uncaptured round leaves it unavailable. Planned work whose ticket no tracker snapshot has shown started is never reported back in the tracker's backlog. Without a runtime nodeMinimum, each check still records the Node it ran and none is marked below a minimum; a record written before checks recorded their Node still validates. Lead publication and candidate processing share the merge queue lock. A temporary flake in the record expires when the base moves. A hand-off can retain its review across lead-authorized base merges. Records without region claims keep whole-file ownership. Records without lane ownership remain readable; an assigned lane on a queued candidate preserves its handing lane and evidence. Without --status-file the live view shows no supervisor banner and renders as before; an unreadable status file shows none. Applied archive digests pin record writers under the state lock. Legacy records remain readable and require a lead writer transition before installed writes. Integration bases merge newer default history through a parked, queue-locked move with applied-archive writer reconciliation and interrupted-publication recovery. A base rerun that was stopped, by a signal or with the runner, journals base.rerun.stopped and puts the candidate back once for each pair of heads, with no base.broken; a second stop at the same heads stops the candidate. The lead names one queued candidate as a broken base's repair: serve takes it alone, and its merge journals base.repaired. The lead's own hold still pauses it. Any base.repaired requeues the candidates that break stopped. Batch members define a check alike when what it runs is alike, whatever its reasons say. A base move after the checks passed carries a check only when the binding's complete readers entries and unread paths show the move changed nothing it reads; without them every check restarts as before. Every delivery on a machine that merges into one base shares that base's merge slot, and a queue command that can't take it within checkTimeoutSeconds attempts nothing and reads queue_locked. A journal entry in the older shape, with a sentence or without facts, is refused and its delivery closes under the release that wrote it. A record given without a story is narrated when it is read. A candidate that adds or removes provenance outputs syncs over a base that only refreshed digests, taking the candidate's listing and regenerating; when both sides changed the listing it stops as before. Once a check of a lone candidate's run has failed, a new hand-off supersedes the rest of that run and any base re-run that follows, on the lead's acceptance, or on the hand-off itself when the delivery needs no acceptance; a batch run is never superseded. The acceptance journals check.superseded, and the queue then stops the checks it started, writes no verdict and never checks the old head again; lead-base-broken names the base broken before a re-run's verdict, with --repair naming another candidate or --self-repair making the failing story's next accepted head the repair; without either, a failed check re-runs on the base as before, and the line map says what a running re-run is for, when it should end and what the lead can do instead. A tracker snapshot without an outside list leaves the record's outside member as it is; a scoped one never adds outside work, and clears only what the sweep itself added, journaled once as work.cleared. A record with no siblings, or a binding with no siblingSnapshot, reconciles and draws as before; a sibling read that is stale, older than snapshotMaxAgeSeconds, unavailable, incompatible or of another epic changes only that sibling's last outcome, and the forge and tracker snapshots beside it still apply. A child a sibling's last kept read lists is left to that sibling, with or without a scope, even while the sibling can't be read; a copy the sweep added earlier is cleared once, journaled as held by that sibling, and a story of this delivery with the same subject is never cleared. A record with no siblings ignores an after key it doesn't hold, as before; with siblings, such a key holds its story as a sibling wait that frees only on a fresh read showing the story landed, and needs the lead only when every same-epic sibling was read fresh; a sibling read that changes nothing writes nothing. A region claim may name its story, and the state tool refuses one naming a story the record doesn't hold; ownership.released, ownership.carried and ownership.carved record what a landing and a carve do to claims, and the queue's ownership check reports every path and hunk outside a lane's claims at once. A record with an integration target carries meta.integration with its base, target and remote; integration.merged, integration.suite, integration.requested and integration.landed record the step into the target, and a review.round under the delivery's own key carries the head it read. A machine directory that can't be created or opened runs work unclaimed and says so, and where the system has no wait4 a claim's slots come from --slots. Every lead wait carries the machine ledger, capacity, running claims, waiters and the last five overrides, or that it can't be read, and wakes the lead once when one of its own delivery's claims has waited past its limit, admitting nothing; the built-in page and the markdown show a Machine section read at render time, left out while no claim is live and no override is recorded, and saying so when the ledger can't be read.

Planning remains complete without optional tracking and reports unavailable optional sensors without replacing repository authority. Nonconverging plan review is not guaranteed to terminate without an operator decision; parallel resources and extension test pins are planned.

Unavailable reviewer evidence remains a failed acquisition; unavailable host cost is explicitly unreported. Unsupported v2 reporting remains explicit; retain selected output without changing delivery authority. Unbounded plan-review rounds are outside the delivery bound and reducer. A lens re-checks each finding it deferred earlier and lists the ones it finds fixed; one it does not list stays deferred.

Lead changes publish under the merge queue lock. A lane can retain its aligned review across exact base commits authorized by the lead before the merge. A temporary flake can be declared while a check runs. The delivery file seeds lane claims and story assignments. The lead can grant disjoint line spans of committed text files in the record. Later lead commands write claims and assignments to the record, and legacy records use the delivery file until explicitly seeded. POSIX hosts only: on Windows the tool exits with a message saying so. Without a forge adapter the lead pushes and opens change requests; without ffmpeg and ffprobe video evidence is unavailable; without Node at the runtime's nodeMinimum first on PATH, which a process and its children run, doctor reports it and lead-init, lead-run and lane-start refuse, even with an nvm Node that meets it; a supervisor started by an older generation records no Node, which doctor --delivery reports as warn; without in-app adapters no in-app checks are declared. A delivery file without criteria writes no plan, and the plan chapter stays off. A delivery without planReview lenses has no plan review, and lead-init freezes its plan as before. Without served integration branches in the binding, a delivery lands on its standing base. Integration setup creates a separate lead checkout and records the standing branch as the target. Without the lead's checkout, view --archive serves an archived copy of the record with the built-in page. Without a tracker adapter, or with tracker.updates set to manual, the lead posts tracker updates by hand; a jira or linear tracker snapshot, or tracker.adapter, posts them through run-delivery's tracker publisher, and a binding whose publisher has a kind and no argv is refused, naming that fix. Without a supervisor (lead-init --no-supervisor, RUN_DELIVERY_SUPERVISOR=off, or one that stopped), the lead's commands do each duty by hand and lead-run --resume starts it again; without the readyPullRequests grant a merge step that refuses drafts gets drafts, and lead-init refuses that. Without a merge script of its own, a binding merges through a shipped forge adapter's merge --source, which merges a branch's one open pull request only at the checked head and refuses anything else. Without tracker.transitions.reviewWhen the lane commands make no review move and print it for the lane instead. The supervisor writes each pass's Needs you list into the record for the line map, and marks it not running when it stops. Without lsof the host can't name a port's listeners, so a starting supervisor never adopts a running live view and starts another, on a free port when the recorded one still answers; a live.json missing leaves the derived port, and a supervisor.json missing, as before any supervisor started or from an older generation's, gives a status line that says the supervisor was not started. Without the generation's host hooks installed, or with a hook set off, no lead's stop is held and no session is oriented: the lead-wait each lead command prints, the status line and Needs you keep the lead's wake. Applied archive digests pin record writers under the state lock. Legacy records remain readable and require a lead writer transition before installed writes. Integration bases merge newer default history through a parked, queue-locked move with applied-archive writer reconciliation and interrupted-publication recovery. A finish line that covers no criteria and no proofs is the lead's to mark, and the supervisor marks a line met once. The close-out files a follow-up only for a finding its lens has not since listed as closed, fixed or withdrawn. A delivery that declares noDeferrals gets a blocker for a finding still deferred at merge, a hand-off refused on an evidence note, and those notes printed at acceptance; without the setting nothing changes. A binding that declares fullHealthRerun has a failed post-merge fullHealth re-checked once: when the tests it names pass alone and nothing in it is a failure the rerun cannot re-check, it journals base.flaky and no base.broken, and repairs nothing; without the member every failed run breaks the base as before. lead-suite runs the binding's fullHealth in a detached checkout of a commit and records the run in the flow log, journalling nothing. Deliveries on one base on a machine list each other in doctor --delivery and the built-in live view, a live view with a configured home lists none, a claim made with lead-own --claim warns another delivery's lead-assign and lead-accept without refusing, and a peer's merge that touches an open story's file journals peer.merged; a delivery alone on its base shows no peers and warns of nothing. lead-push, lead-sync and lead-upgrade-writer take the base's merge slot before the queue lock and refuse with slot_held, naming the holder, when another delivery holds it past their wait. Owned hosted publishing starts or adopts an independent generation-aware watcher, bounds terminal close publication to 30 seconds, retains pending terminal cuts for ten-minute retries and supports credential-free archive viewing with explicit archive retry. Hosted diagnostics report configured hosting before a delivery is selected without reading or creating delivery state; missing credentials and malformed configuration remain explicit. A decision without a reason and a blocker without words are refused before anything is journaled; a kind the registry gives no tracker words posts nothing. A hand-off and the lead's acceptance can name a check whose catalogue entry the candidate's own committed binding adds, before the entry reaches the base; the hand-off marks it as added, and an id in neither catalogue is refused. lead-authorize-base-merge also prints how to finish a merge that stops on a conflict, and a base merge's authorization trailer is read with comment lines dropped, so no git version or comment setting decides whether a review carries; a last merge that lost its trailer is refused with the exact amend that fixes it, and an earlier one is refused with word to merge again. A lane's aligned review carries across an authorized base merge when the story's own change reads the same before and after it, compared both ways hunk by hunk with an appended separator counted as a change, whoever owns the files the base touched; a round a base merge forces counts against the bound. A hand-off is refused when the head conflicts with the current base outside the regenerable paths, or conflicts in a regenerable listing that both sides changed, and names the files and the base-merge command; with base-merge a lane authorizes its own merge of the current base before hand-off, journalled as its own decision, and a merge that leaves the story's change unchanged keeps the aligned review. lead-accept accepts a hand-off that supersedes a failed candidate's run and applies a pending self-repair, and lead-base-broken names the base broken at a head, check and test before a re-run's verdict. Without --scope or --status-state in the binding's tracker snapshot, doctor's tracker snapshot scope row does not apply. lead-sibling refuses a record with no tracker parent and a link that isn't a hosted live view over HTTPS or a loopback test receiver, and doctor names siblings the binding has no siblingSnapshot to read. lead-plan's --after takes a key a same-epic sibling's last read holds, and still refuses one nothing holds; lead-setup notes only an after key that neither the plan nor a known sibling holds. A story's review runs the mandated outcome-correctness and adversarial-testing lenses plus the declared story lenses its lane chooses at round 1 with review-prepare --lenses and --lenses-reason, fixed for its later rounds and shown at hand-off and lead-accept; a lens declared with use plan is never a story lens, and plan review refuses one declared story-only. Without --lenses every declared story lens runs, and with no use declared every declared lens, as before; a story prepared before lenses could be chosen keeps every declared lens. A supervisor child that won't stay up is journalled once as a blocker the lead's wait hears, naming the child, its log and that log's last line, and resolved once the child has stayed up for a pass; a checkout an interrupted lead-suite left under the work folder is removed when its run has ended and nothing works in it, and otherwise recorded as a blocker with the command that removes it, while the merge queue's refusal names it and that command. When a story lands, the region claims granted for it are released, and its lane's other claims on a file the merge changed are carried over the lines the landing changed inside them, or named in Needs you as needing a regrant; a claim that no longer maps doesn't block a grant on its file. lead-own --carve replaces a file's claims whole or changes nothing, a lane's touching claims for one story become one, claims-check lists every line a lane's diff still needs, and lead-claims previews the queue's ownership check. Each supervisor pass reads every assigned lane's pushed story branch from its merge base with the delivery base and writes lane-changes.json beside the record, reading an unchanged branch once; Needs you names each change to a file the lane doesn't hold, or to lines outside its span, without holding the close, a declared shared output raises nothing, and a branch that can't be read is named in place of the lane's items. lead-init writes the integration step for a delivery with an integrationTarget, lead-suite journals integration.suite there with a passed, over-budget, unreadable or failed result, and lead-integrate journals the target merged in, an integration review round, the change request into the target and its merge. Every region grant, carve and carry prints its spans' first and last lines at the base; lead-own --around TEXT names a span by the enclosing function, statement, Markdown section or indented block of the one line holding TEXT, refusing a missing or ambiguous anchor with its candidates; a Python span whose edge cuts a statement is refused; --insert before or after widens a span by one unclaimed line so an insertion at its edge falls inside it; and claims-check asks for spans by anchor. A close leaves an operator's checkout that is on another branch or holds uncommitted changes where it is, naming why, and lead-retire keeps the lead's checkout, naming what holds it, while anything of the delivery runs from it, the archive lacks a journal entry, or it holds a change or an unpushed head. Claiming commands, claim, check, gate, lead-push's guards, lead-suite and the post-merge fullHealth, run unclaimed and say so when the machine ledger can't be used.
